title: Traffic-suture cutover with per-connection circuit brokers and stream-preserving load quarantine
creator: Marco Delgado
description: Problem: During active-active multi-region failovers we observe prolonged streaming session disconnects, token duplication on replays, and amplification of tail latency when regional egress is drained aggressively. Goal: Implement a coordinated 'traffic-suture' cutover mechanism at the edge that stitches live streaming sessions across regions, employs per-connection circuit brokers to apply weighted shedding, and provides a quarantined slowdown lane for degraded hosts to avoid global latency tail amplification. The feature must preserve session continuity for streaming consumers where possible, maintain overall P95/P99 latency SLOs, and reduce client-visible errors during regional failover by >= 90% compared to current drain behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Active-active cutover can move 100% of new connections from region A->B with <200ms median extra handshake latency
In-flight streaming sessions that opt into handover experience no more than 2 reconnection attempts on average
During simulated regional drain, global P95 token latency increase limited to <= 15% and P99 limited to <= 30%
Circuit broker enforces per-connection drop rates configured by policy and exposes metrics for per-key shedding
Canary rollout completes with no customer-facing errors in 3 representative accounts and automated rollback triggers on SLO regression
design_summary: Introduce a lightweight edge-side coordinator (Traffic Suture Controller) that: 1) tags streaming connections with a migration token and preferred handoff target region; 2) negotiates a short-lived proxy stitch for streaming sockets during cutover using ephemeral forwarding tunnels; 3) consults per-connection Circuit Brokers for graceful shedding decisions based on connection priority, token cache health, and SLO headroom. The controller integrates with the existing Smart Router to update routing policy atomically and publishes telemetry to the console for per-route SLO dashboards. Fallback: non-opted streams follow the existing drain + reconnect path.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Complexity increase at the edge (new coordination state) — mitigated by a small GC-friendly state machine and bounded TTL for migration tokens
Slightly higher memory usage per connection for stitch metadata; measured projected 3-5% increase under peak — acceptable for Dedicated/hosted tiers
Risk of token replay/duplication during partial handoff — mitigated by idempotent token checks in the receiving region and short-lived leases
Operational surface: new metrics and dashboards needed to avoid blind spots during early rollouts
If circuit brokers are too aggressive, we may reduce availability for low-priority customers; policy defaults must be conservative
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flags + simulation harness in staging (unit tests + integration against synthetic load) - 2 weeks
Phase 1: Internal canary on infra team traffic with telemetry enabled - 3 days
Phase 2: 10% hosted traffic across low-risk tenants via gradual ramp controlled by SLO monitors - 1 week
Phase 3: 50% ramp with targeted streams opt-in (client SDK header) + runbook for rollback - 1 week
Phase 4: Global enable for hosted with per-account opt-out and per-route policies - post-verification
qa_and_testing: Add synthetic streaming scenarios to chaos tests (packet loss, region partition, control plane lag)
Run distributed soak tests with millions of short-lived and long-lived streams to validate memory and stitch success rates
Fuzz migration token lifecycle to catch idempotency and replay cases
Load test Circuit Broker policy variations to calibrate conservative defaults
End-to-end smoke with Redwood SDK streaming client and a set of customer-like prompts
monitoring_and_alerting: New console dashboards: traffic_suture.success_rate, traffic_suture.handshake_latency_ms, circuit_broker.drop_fraction, stitch_replay_errors
SLO probes: synthetic P95/P99 token latency and streaming continuity checks per-region
Alert: traffic_suture.success_rate < 98% for 5m triggers rollback playbook
Alert: circuit_broker.drop_fraction > configured_threshold for > 1m triggers policy scale review
implementation_notes: Edge controller implemented in Rust to reuse existing runtime kernel bindings; lightweight RPC to regional ingress via mTLS
Migration token TTL: 20s by default; configurable per-release; issued by origin gateway
Stitch tunnel: shortlist to HTTP/2 proxying or ephemeral websocket pass-through depending on client type
Circuit Broker policy evaluated per-connection using scored heuristics (priority, token-age, kv-cache-hit-rate, route-level SLO headroom)
Expose a runtime config for immediate global 'quarantine' enabling to send degraded hosts into slow lane
